OUTSOURCING SEO

Outsourcing SEO: A Guide for UK Businesses

A buyer-focused guide to outsourcing SEO, defining responsibilities and choosing the right level of support.

By Cyberfreak Software · 28 November 2026

Start with the work you need help with

“SEO” can mean technical diagnosis, content planning, local optimisation, link acquisition, implementation or measurement. Before you outsource SEO, identify the task that is currently going undone. A focused brief helps you find a suitable specialist and stops a small monitoring need from turning into an oversized retainer.

Decide who owns implementation

Some businesses want an agency to make changes directly. Others have a developer or marketing colleague who can act on recommendations. Agree who has access to the website, who approves changes and how urgent issues are handled. If the provider is advisory, recommendations should be specific enough for the person implementing them to understand.

Set a sensible reporting rhythm

A useful update connects completed work with observable evidence: Search Console clicks, impressions, queries and indexing where relevant. It should explain what changed, what needs attention and what the next action is. Avoid reports that present a dashboard without interpretation or treat rankings as the only measure of success.

Check fit before signing

Ask for a written scope, named deliverables, access requirements, communication expectations, pricing and cancellation terms. Ask what is excluded as well as what is included. You should retain ownership of your domain, website, analytics and Search Console accounts.
